This file is a REPOSITORY record; it is not part of any package. It covers
the third-party source the repository carries to build its two distributed
programs, dx and wasm-bindgen:

            https://crates.io/crates/dioxus-cli
            (https://github.com/DioxusLabs/dioxus); the pristine archive is in
            tools/dx-native-tools/vendoring/dioxus-cli
  License:  MIT OR Apache-2.0; used under Apache-2.0
  Changes:  this copy is MODIFIED. The changes are the seven numbered patch
            files in tools/dx-native-tools/vendoring/dioxus-cli and are
            described in PATCH-NOTES.txt there. Each changed place in the
            source carries a comment that starts "CodeBrix change:".

libgit2-sys stand-in, ours (declarations taken from upstream)
  Where:    tools/dx-native-tools/sources/codebrix-libgit2-sys
  Origin:   the repository's own crate. Its lib.rs is lib.rs of the
            crates.io crate libgit2-sys 0.18.3+1.9.2
            (https://github.com/rust-lang/git2-rs), with three changes marked
            "CodeBrix change:"; nothing else of that crate was taken - in
            particular not its libgit2/ folder (libgit2's C source), which
            this repository never carries. README.txt there is its notice.
  License:  MIT OR Apache-2.0 (upstream's LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE,
            verbatim, beside it)

wasm-split-cli (dx's WebAssembly bundle splitter), modified
  Where:    tools/dx-native-tools/sources/wasm-split-cli
  Origin:   the wasm-split-cli crate, version 0.7.10,
            https://crates.io/crates/wasm-split-cli
            (https://github.com/DioxusLabs/dioxus); the pristine archive is in
            tools/dx-native-tools/vendoring/wasm-split-cli
  License:  MIT OR Apache-2.0; used under Apache-2.0
  Changes:  this copy is MODIFIED by the two numbered patch files in
            tools/dx-native-tools/vendoring/wasm-split-cli, described in
            PATCH-NOTES.txt there; dx's Cargo.toml puts it in place of the
            crates.io crate, which is therefore not in the vendor folder.
            Each changed place carries a comment that starts "CodeBrix
            change:".

wasm-bindgen CLI, unmodified
  Where:    tools/dx-native-tools/sources/wasm-bindgen-cli
  Origin:   the wasm-bindgen-cli crate, version 0.2.130,

The Rust crates the two are built from, every one of them, are listed below
with their licenses. They are in tools/dx-native-tools/sources/vendor, exactly

distributed program; what is, on each of the five platforms, is recorded in

================================================================================
Rust crates vendored for the build tools
================================================================================
These crates build the two tools whose source is in tools/dx-native-tools/sources: the Dioxus
CLI (dx) and the wasm-bindgen CLI. Their source is in tools/dx-native-tools/sources/vendor, unmodified.
This part includes crates under the Mozilla Public License 2.0, which is accepted in the build
tools' tree; thirteen of them build the distributed dx (ten are compiled into it, three are
procedural macros) and are accepted for that by name. What is compiled into each distributed
program is recorded in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES-Dioxus.txt and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES-WasmBindgen.txt
beside this file, which travel with the programs.

[T0153] openssl-src 300.6.1+3.6.3: openssl/util/perl/OpenSSL/copyright.pm
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#! /usr/bin/env perl
# Copyright 2021-2022 The OpenSSL Project Authors. All Rights Reserved.
#
# Licensed under the Apache License 2.0 (the "License").  You may not use
# this file except in compliance with the License.  You can obtain a copy
# in the file LICENSE in the source distribution or at
# https://www.openssl.org/source/license.html

use strict;
use warnings;

package OpenSSL::copyright;

sub year_of {
    my $file = shift;

    return $ENV{'OSSL_COPYRIGHT_YEAR'} if defined $ENV{'OSSL_COPYRIGHT_YEAR'};

    # Get the current year.  We use that as the default because the other
    # common case is that someone unpacked a tarfile and the file dates
    # are't properly set on extract.
    my $YEAR = [localtime()]->[5] + 1900;

    # See if git's available
    open my $FH,
       "git log -1 --date=short --format=format:%cd $file 2>/dev/null|"
           or return $YEAR;
    my $LINE = <$FH>;
    close $FH;
    $LINE =~ s/^([0-9]*)-.*/$1/;
    $YEAR = $LINE if $LINE;
    return $YEAR;
}

sub latest {
    my $l = 0;
    foreach my $f (@_ ) {
        my $y = year_of($f);
        $l = $y if $y > $l;
    }
    return $l
}
1;
